match.reason: No existing point teaches the forces that push a business to change; the environment and influence points cover related factors but not change itself, so this needs a new point.

draft.title: Forces for change
card: A force for change is something that pushes a business to change how it operates. Forces can come from outside the business or from inside it.
come from the business environment, outside its control. Examples are new technology, competitors, changes in the law and changing customer tastes.
come from within the business. Examples are a new manager with new ideas, poor financial results, and low staff morale.
A force pushes a business to consider change. The business still decides how, and whether, to respond.
draft.remember: Forces for change can come from outside the business or from inside it, and the business decides how to respond.

a.q: Which of these is an internal force for change in a business?
opts: Falling profits that worry the owners
A new competitor opening nearby
A new law on workplace safety
A new app that customers prefer to use
a.why: Falling profits are a result inside the business, so they are an internal force. A new competitor, a new law and new technology all come from outside the business, so they are external forces.
a.clue: Which one comes from inside the business, not its surroundings?

b.q: Mia owns a bakery in Dubbo. A new supermarket opens nearby and sells cheap bread. Mia's sales drop, and she begins to change her menu. Which statement is correct?
opts: The supermarket is external and the fall in sales is internal
Both the supermarket and the sales fall are external
The supermarket is internal and the fall in sales is external
Both the supermarket and the sales fall are internal
b.why: The supermarket is a competitor outside the bakery, so it is an external force. The fall in sales shows up in the bakery's own results, so it is an internal force. Calling both external is tempting because the supermarket caused the drop, but the poor result is still inside Mia's business.
b.clue: Ask where each force comes from: outside the bakery or in its own results.

problems.detail: The sales fall is caused directly by the external competitor. A careful teacher could argue it is the effect of one external force rather than a separate internal force, which makes 'Both ... are external' defensible. The stem could make the internal force more independent, for example by adding a separate internal cause, or ask only about the supermarket.
